cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Can You Keep It?
cards.instruction: Use increasingly sensitive details to test whether someone deserves deeper trust.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The club's changing the menu. Keep that quiet; I'll handle the announcement.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I won't tell anyone. Can I still complain about the old one?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Complain all you like. The chef's leaving; don't let that slip while you do.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then I'd better stop asking Sam who she wants cooking next season.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll talk to Sam. I'm taking over the kitchen; tell me what you've said before I tell you who's coming with me.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 controls low-stakes menu disclosure; A3 permits ordinary complaints but adds chef departure; A5 reveals takeover while withholding team names pending an account of B talk, keeping deeper trust conditional.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 complaint permission does not imply disclosure of new plans; B4 previous questions may invite speculation, so A5 asks what was said rather than declaring an actual leak.

relationship.evidence: B2 checks what ordinary speech remains permitted and B4 identifies a risky habit without being accused by an omniscient narrator.

heightening.evidence: B4 Sam questions cause A5 to take that contact and demand an account before the next sensitive names.

specificity.evidence: A1 club menu, A3 chef departure and A5 takeover establish increasing sensitivity and the concrete next test.
